sampling_model.design: An independent sample \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is drawn from the selected multinomial law \(q\); an optional COPAG confidence set is produced from the same sample by a coverage-valid discovery procedure.
sampling_model.units: Each sampled unit is one retained clinical visit with finite coded variables \(V\); the population SCM also contains the binary selection variable \(S\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query is the hard intervention \(do(B=b)\); the intervention is hypothetical and sampling randomness comes from the selected observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every selected cell is positive under \(q\). The common lower bound \(\delta\) on population and post-intervention selection is a calibrated sensitivity restriction, not a standard overlap label; the conditional estimand itself only requires \(d_M>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(q\) by a simultaneous multinomial confidence region and propagate graph uncertainty by union over a COPAG confidence set; no faithfulness assumption is imposed on the identification class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 equates a fixed canonical-DAG discrete causal bounding problem with minimization and maximization of a polynomial program.
Theorem 3 states that optimal neural counterfactual bounds and optimal PAG counterfactual bounds coincide under a faithful observational law.
Theorem 4.13 gives equality of marginal DAG models for DAGs with the same latent projection, and Proposition 7.3 commutes intervention with projection.
Proposition 2 replaces one latent source by at most \(d+1\) values without changing the observed network behavior.
Equality of selected-marginalized directed graphs is equivalent to indistinguishability under the Observe-and-Do probing scheme.
Theorem 4.15 gives completeness of sIDP and the causal calculus for unconditional interventional kernels under a COPAG.
Theorem 5 states that faithful distributions are nonempty, open, and dense in the total-variation Markov model.
Criterion inversion yields consistent set estimators, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets defined by population minimizers.
Width-adaptive endpoint intervals attain uniform asymptotic coverage for an interval-identified scalar as the identification width approaches zero.
Resampling and screening followed by a union of graph-specific intervals gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after causal discovery.

body.tldr: The note constructs a bounded finite graph-legal response fiber using at most \(N!\) saturated order-indexed super-architectures.  Essential-feature signs encode absent and active arrows and sources, and one-block real-algebraic procedures return endpoint witnesses or certificates excluding a value from every bounded branch with singly exponential dependence on the response-program dimension.  These certificates concern only the bounded finite image: equality with the arbitrary-SCM fiber, closure, and universal endpoint attainment remain open for positive, potentially unfaithful selected laws.  Independently of graph restrictions, consistency and the two calibrated \(\delta\)-margins give a universal closed-form outer envelope; one-source exact complete-COPAG models attain it, so every permitted-graph class containing those witnesses inherits the exact interval.  The binary law \(q=(1,2,3,4)/10\) at \(\delta=1/4\) yields \([1/20,39/40]\) as an audit instance for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery analysis of Lee et al., not as the headline.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm on specified model classes; Yang et al. optimize over faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; Duarte et al. optimize a fixed canonical DAG; and Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models. None settles whether the exact actual-parent COPAG fiber for a positive, potentially unfaithful selected law is closed or has attained endpoints. This note also leaves that general question open, while formalizing it and proving bounded-finite and saturated special-case results.
project_justification.niche: The tractable object constructed here is the bounded finite graph-legal response fiber, a finite union of semialgebraic strata. Its essential-feature signs determine the exact selected MAG, and real-algebraic procedures decide whether a boundary value of this bounded image has a legal representative or is excluded from all bounded branches. Equality with, and closure or attainment of, the full arbitrary-SCM fiber remain exactly \(\text{oeq:universal-legal-lifting}\).
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and if-and-only-if legality test, embeds sparse response models into at most \(N!\) saturated ordered super-architectures, and gives a singly exponential one-block certificate procedure for the bounded finite image.  It proves a graph-independent universal selection-margin envelope with attained one-source endpoints in the exact complete-COPAG subclass, designates the compelled-collider case as the first unresolved kill test for universal lifting, and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence.

body.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning.  Evans canonicalizes margins of latent DAGs and relates latent projection to intervention, but this does not preserve an exact functional-essentiality stratum under moment compression.  Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give network hidden-variable cardinality bounds; their sourcewise reduction motivates the finite support step but does not preserve strict actual-edge witnesses.  Duarte et al. fix a canonical DAG and optimize over graph-permitted finite NPSEMs, without requiring every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.  Yang et al. treat faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; their edge semantics and the actual-parent, potentially unfaithful selected-MAG semantics here are generally incomparable.  Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models, whereas the present margins constrain absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities.  Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm or calculus on specified classes and distinguish \(\mathcal M(G)\) from the positive discrete class \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); positivity of the selected observed law \(q\) here is not equated with all positivity conditions defining \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  Boeken, Forr\'e, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not supply an equal-moment lift at an unfaithful boundary.  Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky motivate confidence-set inversion, while the formal inference result here is only finite-sample outer coverage.  Lee et al. are the clinical consumer: their survivor-conditioned cardiac-surgery analysis uses FCI and LV-IDA under acknowledged selection bias and graph ambiguity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Saturated order-indexed super-architectures eliminate redundant subset enumeration, but they do not close the legality topology.  In the positive binary exclusive-or family, moment-preserving support deletion can send a shared-source essentiality polynomial to zero while holding the selected law and intervention moment fixed.  An equal-moment legal lift exists in that example, so it is a warning against naive compression rather than a negative answer.  More generally, a bounded-compiler exclusion certificate does not exclude a repair outside the finite support bound.
body.honest_scope: Established results cover child-set source merging within the retained-variable response language, moment-preserving sourcewise finite support on a fixed permitted architecture, embedding into at most \(N!\) saturated ordered super-architectures, exact polynomial legality for bounded finite response models, singly exponential existential-semialgebraic endpoint certification for that bounded image, a universal selection-margin outer envelope with exact complete-COPAG subclass attainment, and finite-sample confidence-fiber event inclusion.  Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded compiler, preservation of exact actual-parent semantics through arbitrary canonicalization or compression, and closure or attainment of the full positive-unfaithful COPAG fiber remain open.  No general endpoint-convergence claim is made.  The interval \([1/20,39/40]\) is a binary audit instance; it is not evidence for universal lifting.
body.interpretation: The closed-form envelope is a universal partial-identification statement derived from consistency, selected-law fit, bounded outcomes, and the two calibrated selection margins; graph assumptions enter only when proving endpoint attainment by a permitted witness subclass.  By contrast, the algebraic endpoint procedure characterizes the bounded finite graph-legal image exactly.  A positive certificate is an attained bounded-model mechanism, while a negative certificate says only that every bounded branch fails and must not be reported as nonattainment over arbitrary SCMs.
